why: We back technical founders whose software changes how a whole industry works. Right now this is a meal-plan app sitting on top of one grocer, and when we asked what nobody could copy, there was no answer.
fix: Name the software you own that a delivery app or a grocer's own app could not copy in a quarter, and show it running: the planner logic, the cart-filling data, or a link into the grocer's systems.
Say which founder owns the core tech and put that person up front. Then explain why software is the moat if the $500K only hires one engineer.
Show that adding a grocery chain is a software job you can repeat quickly, not a new deal from scratch each time, so this can change how families buy food and not just plug into one store.

quotes.words: What a delivery app or grocer could not copy: [not answered]
quotes.note: This is our main question and it went unanswered. With no moat on record, this looks like a feature a grocer could add to its own app.

quotes.words: Who owns the core tech, and why only one engineer: [not answered]
quotes.note: We can't tell who the technical founder is, and an ask for 'one engineer' makes the software sound small.

quotes.words: One built the meal planner at a food delivery company.
quotes.note: The strongest point in the pitch: real experience building the product. But it was never connected to anything only this team can build.

quotes.words: Works with one grocery chain today
quotes.note: Relying on one partner is the opposite of changing an industry. The grocer controls the channel, not Tidy.
